title: Continual Queue Smoother and Kernel Adjudicator
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Summary: Implement a two-part runtime feature: (1) a Continual Queue Smoother (CQS) that dampens microburst arrival variance using a credit-based pacing window and EMA service-time model; (2) a Kernel Adjudicator (KA) that selects and probes kernel paths at slot reservation time based on a low-cost microbenchmark and lightweight attention shape hashing. Goal: reduce 99th-percentile end-to-end latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads by 20-30% under typical tail bursts, while preserving median throughput and keeping token-cost delta < 3%.
detailed_goals: 1) Reduce 99p latency for small/medium sequences (<512 tokens) on T4/GPU mixes by 20% in production canary. 2) Eliminate cascading queue spikes caused by sudden prefill storms via CQS burst credits. 3) Add a <500us kernel probe with KA to avoid full-decoder stalls when switching attention kernel paths. 4) Expose telemetry for kernel-choice, probe latency, credit drawdown, and contention events in Console routes dashboard.
background: We still see recurring tail-latency events when a mix of short prefill-heavy and long decode-heavy requests arrive simultaneously. Existing admission heuristics are reactive and maintain separate prefill/decode queues, causing kernel warmup penalties and suboptimal kernel path choices for attention-heavy sequences. Prior tickets implemented admission shapers and speculative slot reservations, but gaps remain: (a) microbursts cause sudden queue depth that stalls kernel handovers, (b) kernel selection is often stale because it uses profile metadata only, not runtime microbenchmarks.
approach: - Continual Queue Smoother: implement per-GPU token-credit buckets that refill at a rate tuned per-instance based on smoothed arrival rate and historical service time. Credits are consumed when admitting prefill or decode slots; when exhausted, CQS applies soft backpressure (delayed admission) instead of hard rejection. - Kernel Adjudicator: on slot reservation, compute an attention-shape hash and run a sub-millisecond microprobe kernel on a tiny synthetic batch to measure effective throughput for the candidate kernel variants. Cache adjudications keyed by (model-version, attention-hash, hw-tag) with time-to-live and stale-eviction. If probe latency > threshold, fallback to fast conservative kernel or trigger low-latency hedging (speculative second slot). - Tail hedging: when probe indicates a large variance or high contention, KA can trigger speculative decode slot assignment on a warm GPU with risk-limited duplication and automatic dedup on first-token emission.
tradeoffs: - Microprobes add a small extra GPU work item; we limit probe frequency via caching and TTLs to avoid throughput erosion. - Credit-based smoothing delays some admissions intentionally; this can slightly increase median latency for opportunistic low-priority requests but prevents large tail spikes impacting higher-priority traffic. - Speculative hedging increases ephemeral token cost; capped duplication and cost telemetry ensure we keep token-cost delta under control.
success_criteria: - 99p latency improvement >=20% on canary cluster under synthetic burst tests. - No more than 3% increase in token spend at production QPS. - Kernel-choice mismatch rate (post-adjudication vs optimal offline) <5%. - Dashboard metrics (kernel_probe_latency, credit_drawdown, hedged_requests) exist and are queryable.
plan: 1) Spike implementation of KA microprobe and cache (week 1). 2) Implement CQS token buckets + admission hooks (week 2). 3) Integrate hedging policy and throttles (week 3). 4) Unit/integration tests + canary rollout (week 4). 5) 2-week canary monitoring and rollback window, iterate on thresholds (weeks 5-6).
risks: - Probe misclassification under multi-tenant noisy neighbors could cause suboptimal kernel picks. Mitigation: require multiple consistent probes before a persistent kernel flip and backoff under high contention. - Incorrect credit refill tuning could starve low-priority tenants. Mitigation: expose tenant-priority weights and emergency burst allowances. - Complexity in dedup/hedge flow may introduce edge-case double-response bugs; will add strict idempotency checks and end-to-end tests.
testing: - Synthetic burst harness (existing tool) to generate prefill+decode mixes with controlled arrival jitter. - Kernel microprobe simulator to validate probe TTL and cache behavior. - Load tests on canary GPU pool with golden PROM queries for 99p and p50 comparisons. - QA: integration test validating single-request idempotency under speculative hedging and dedup.
rollout: Phase 0: internal dev cluster (toggle off by default). Phase 1: canary on 2% production load with enhanced telemetry. Phase 2: progressive ramp to 50% with automatic rollback triggers (99p spike > baseline*1.5 or token-cost delta >3%). Phase 3: full rollout with monitoring alerts and runbook updates.
observability_and_alerting: Add metrics: kernel_adjudicator.probe_latency_ms, kernel_adjudicator.choice, cqs.credit_level, cqs.rejected_admissions, hedging. Alerts: probe_latency_p95 > 2ms, credit_replenish_rate drop >30%, hedged_request_rate > configured_threshold. Dashboards: per-model route breakdown and GPU-instance heatmaps.
